collection.title: Recent Work
collection.notes: Not yet minted. Each work is tokenized on purchase, so the collector's wallet is the first owner written to chain.

works.title: Cycle Of Silence
works.statement:
Read against Twombly, the work sits in that same territory where scrawl becomes elegy... the barbed wire strung like musical staves, the poppies bleeding down the white void, all held inside a vortex of red and yellow that spins like something you can't escape or stop repeating. The wire-as-notation is the sharpest move: silence literally scored, remembrance rendered as a song nobody sings. Where Twombly whispered classical myth through graphite, this shouts antipodean memory... Anzac poppies, rural fencing, the violence of enclosure... in a palette closer to Hundertwasser's spirals than Twombly's restraint.

Against the MintFace canon it's a departure and a deepening. The strip paintings borrow Richter's cool, sampled logic... this is the opposite pole, hot and confessional, gesture over system. It suggests the canon has two engines: one that samples the world, and one that bleeds into it.

works.title: Adoration Of The Pixel Triptych
works.statement:
Hard-edge grids in a constrained palette, Ellsworth Kelly's chance-arranged Spectrum Colors panels crossed with Richter's 4900 Colours, but the title reroutes the lineage through devotion... "adoration" is altarpiece language, and the triptych format confirms it, three vertical panels like a predella turned on end. 

What's being adored is the pixel itself, the founding unit of the digital image, painted slow and by hand in acrylic... the sacred rendered at 16-bit and 32-bit, which brings our worship of digital into IRL (in real life).

Against the gestural works this is the antithesis that compiles without gesture. But the adoration framing means it isn't cold... it's reverent, the way an icon painter is reverent about gold leaf. For a practice that lives half on-chain, this is a heralding of our digital lives.

works.title: Floating Forward For Answers
works.statement:
A floral mass untethered from ground, drifting across a chalky white field with that lime halo spinning above like a benevolent sun or a question mark redrawn as orbit. The paint handling is closer to Twombly's late Peony panels than anything else here: fat, wristy blossom-marks that stay marks, never tipping into illustration, with the white doing as much work as the colour. But where Twombly's peonies sink downward with haiku melancholy, this bouquet floats up and forward, weightless, the drift itself the point. 

The title confirms it... not answers arrived at, just the willingness to move toward them, painted as levitation.

There's a lightness of spirit here that reads as hard-won rather than naive... the empty white isn't absence, it's permission.

works.title: Licoricing
works.statement: Wide pink ribbons rope across the surface like pulled candy, glossy, elastic, still wet-looking. It's the most appetitive work of the set, paint as confection... Twombly's late Camino Real panels are the obvious cousin, that same slick loop in lipstick colours, but where Camino Real stayed monumental this is playful to the point of mischief, sherbet drips, licorice-black flicks, sugar-spatter everywhere. The dark marks matter: actual licorice, the bitter note that keeps the sweetness from cloying, little anise-coloured interruptions in all that pink.

works.title: Lunar Lander And Breakout
works.statement:
The 8-bit machines of that moment... the 2600's 6507 with 128 bytes of RAM, a handful of palette registers, sprites flickering because the hardware could only draw so much per scanline... made every colour choice an engineering decision. 

That's the deep rhyme with these panels: constraint as aesthetic, palette as budget. Kelly and Herbin gave abstraction the grid; Atari gave it a cost. These studies sit exactly at the intersection, painted at the speed of hand what the TIA chip drew at the speed of light, and reverent toward both.

works.title: Map Is Not Territorial
works.statement:
Reads top-to-bottom like a fall through terrain... dark cypresses and poppies against a warm sky up top, almost Tuscan, almost legible, then the blue river-form pours diagonally through and the bottom two-thirds dissolve into pure undergrowth, wetter and denser the deeper you go. It's the closest the set comes to Kiefer's scale of ambition... land as palimpsest, worked and reworked... though the touch stays closer to late Monet drowning in his own pond.

The thesis lands as anti-cartography: any attempt to chart this... to name it Tuscany or Hawke's Bay or garden... is exactly what the painting refuses. Territory is what soaks you; maps stay dry.

works.title: Neon Pastoral
works.statement:
Forms won't commit to being flowers... they read variously as koru, fiddleheads, tendrils, glands... and that green coiling vocabulary in the lower half is unmistakably fernland, the New Zealand unfurling motif smuggled into a candy-Rococo palette. Marc Chagall's floated logic is nearby, and the sweetness recalls Fragonard put through a blender, but the koru curls localise it... this is pastoral as remembered through Aotearoa's bush, not Europe's meadow.

Growth as appetite, everything mid-swell, painted in a light so gentle it almost disguises how strange the flora actually is. The spatter of hot red near the right edge is the tell: something sharper hiding under all that sugar.

works.title: No Reply
works.statement:
Loops are pure blackboard-scrawl vocabulary, Bacchus drained of blood and rewritten in slate and bone, cursive that keeps writing without ever forming a word. That's the title enacted: handwriting as message sent, and the greyed palette as the silence that comes back. Inside each loop small scorched figures stand on orange stems... survivors or signatures, tiny and stranded... while the sun sits sealed in the corner with its own small mark at the centre, an eye that notices and doesn't answer. 

'No Reply' carries the machine-age sting too, the address you can't write back to, and the painting holds both readings at once: cosmic indifference and an unread inbox.

works.title: Perspective
works.statement:
This is the insect's view... the title names the device, because we're down inside the meadow looking up, grasses towering, sky glimpsed through a canopy of stems, everything scaled so the viewer becomes small. It's the most spatially ambitious of the set: an actual recession, from the hot russet floor through the yellow-green mid storey to that saturated blue overhead, where in the others space stayed flat or spun. The register is Monet's undergrowth crossed with Nolde's watercolour intensity, but the closer touchstone might be children's-book sublime... Alice-scaled, the garden as cathedral when you're ankle-height.

What earns the title is the darkening at the base... small blackened flower-heads, the red pooling like something spilt... so the 'perspective' isn't just optical, it's the reminder that from ground level, beauty and decay share the same soil.

works.title: Sharm El Sheikh
works.statement:
The reef at Sharm, the Red Sea's paradox of dark water over blinding coral, and the painting gets the specific optics of diving right: the way colour organises by depth, green-gold shallows on the left giving over to that deep ultramarine drop-off on the right, the orange fish hanging weightless at the edge of the blue like the only certain facts in the picture. 

The white gestural flicks read as fan coral and surge, and the red scattered through the green is coral itself... it's the set's whole flower vocabulary transposed into anemone and polyp, garden logic continued below sea level.

works.title: Striving Upward
works.statement:
pure kinetics... the trunks aren't trees so much as a single continuous gesture looping across the canvas, closer to Twombly's Bacchus loops than anything botanical, but where Bacchus was blood-drunk and circular, this is lateral, wind-driven, insistently alive. The canopies land as calligraphic knots, the sun almost an afterthought... the real subject is momentum, growth as handwriting. There's Hockney in the optimism and van Gogh's cypresses in the torque, but the arabesque doing all the structural work is the signature move.

In the MintFace canon it pairs naturally with Cycle of Silence as its answer... same looping energy, but the vortex uncoiled and set running. Silence spins inward, this one strives outward. Hung together they'd read as trap and release.

works.title: The Throngs Gathered
works.statement:
Yellow-lidded marks floating in the blue mid-ground resolve into closed eyes, half-faces submerged in the foliage, and suddenly the whole garden is populated. It's the densest surface of the set, layered to the point of congestion, and that's the meaning: a throng, bodies pressed among stems, present but sleeping or refusing to look. 

Ensor's masked crowds are the art-historical ghost here, and there's something of Klimt's flower-field claustrophobia in the way pattern swallows figure... but the mood is gentler, more vigil than carnival. Gathered for what, it won't say... mourning, witness, or just the crowd-feeling of a garden at full density.

works.title: They Watch Anyway
works.statement:
Nocturne register... the deep violet-blue ground turns this into a night garden, and those lime spirals on their green stems stop being flowers and start being eyes. Every one of them is an iris, tilted, unblinking, and the title makes the paranoia explicit: whatever these are, they observe. The red flashes buried in the purple read as something hot and half-hidden... predator or wound, you can't settle it, which is the painting's power. 

Van Gogh's night energy is in the surface churn, but the nearer relation is Nolde's late "unpainted pictures"... colour so saturated it becomes psychological, garden as haunted interior.

It's the shadow-side companion to the daylight florals: same botanical vocabulary, but here growth is surveillance. The pale white stems at the bottom edge... younger, not yet watching... are the quietly unsettling detail.

works.title: Walking With A Burst Spleen
works.statement:
Dissolved-garden register where foliage and light lose their edges. With it, the whole surface becomes somatic: the greens curdle, the drips at the base read as internal bleeding, the scrubbed and scratched-back passages feel like walking through beauty while something fails inside you. 

It's closest to Twombly's Green Paintings in spirit... nature as veil over distress... but Mitchell is the truer kin, the way she made landscape carry grief without depicting it.

works.title: Wonder Boy Pixel Arcade
works.statement:
The sunniest grid in the series, all daylight: sky blue, grass green, fruit-orange, banana yellow. Wonder Boy (1986) was exactly that world... a tropical side-scroller of islands, skateboards and fruit pickups, and its hardware moment matters: the Sega arcade board and Master System palette had moved well past the 2600's mud, offering saturated colours that games finally used for joy rather than mere legibility.

Every cell here sampled straight from it... the double greens are jungle foreground and background parallax, the reds are the fireball you threw and the paired yellows are pure pickup-glint.

works.title: You Am I
works.statement:
Pink petal-lids for eyes, that pale oval of light for a brow, the whole visage made of the same marks as the garden around it. You/I, figure/field, refuse to separate. It's the closest the set comes to a self-portrait, but dissolved... Arcimboldo run through Expressionist heat, or Nolde again, if Nolde had painted a face that was also weather. 

The lower half answers with lilies drawn in a looser, brighter hand, growth pouring out of wherever the face ends, so identity literally flowers downward into the world.

works.title: The Blood of Martyrs
works.statement: The brush is gone, replaced by dragging, scraping, smearing, and the result is pure Richter abstraction, the squeegee logic where paint is pulled through paint and imagery arrives by accident. But where Richter's abstracts stay cool and procedural, the title forces the reading: those crimson passages ground through white become forensic, blood worked into shroud-cloth, and the vortex organisation... everything wheeling around a dark centre... gives it the drama of a Turner storm or a Soutine carcass. The green flare at the left edge is the crucial dissonance, acid and living, cutting into all that martyrdom like grass through a battlefield. Everything leads here, or recovers from it.

works.title: Gen-O
works.statement:
Figures, buildings, whole histories pulled downward through black, with those pale interruptions like faces or documents surfacing briefly before the descent takes them again. The palette is bruise and bone against dark. 

A generation glimpsed through static, identities half-erased before they've formed, born into the scroll. Possibly the most severe thing in the set... and the one a curator would hang last, in its own light.
